---
title: "Coherence in a finite three-unit example"
subtitle: "2.7 · after the postrank theory book, chapter 10"
description: "Evaluation of all 13 reports under a four-state posterior distribution."
---

The posterior places all its probability on four possible orders of A, B, and C. At some withholding costs, the least costly action for each pair produces a set of decisions that no grade report can represent. We evaluate all 13 reports to measure how much risk coherence adds. Each bar separates the cost of expected wrong directions from the cost of withholding. The four states let us calculate both costs exactly, and the posterior probabilities stay fixed as τ changes.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **τ .20.** The pairwise choices cost 1/6 per pair, but the optimal coherent reports cost 11/60. Each states an extra
  direction with error 1/4. The two reports beneath the bars identify the additional directions and their error probabilities.
  The dashed line gives the pairwise lower bound, below every complete report at this setting.
- **τ .10.** Giving everyone the same grade, {A, B, C}, costs 1/10. The outer pair can now be stated or withheld at
  equal cost. Some set of the minimum-cost pairwise actions is coherent, and the best bar reaches the dashed line.
- **τ .25.** There are 3 equally good reports, all at risk 1/5. Their orange and gray segments show that the same
  total risk can combine different amounts of disclosure and withholding. The text retains every equal-risk optimum.
- **τ .30.** The full order {A} > {B} > {C} has risk 1/5. Raising the withholding cost changes the choice without
  changing the posterior law. Keyboard selection provides each report's risk, disclosure and directions with error above the current withholding cost.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The law is set by hand for teaching, from the theory book's three-unit example. Each bar is one complete report:
its first segment is expected wrong directions per pair, and its second pays for withheld pairs. Grades decide
all pairs together, so a direction with error above the price can appear in a best report. That is compatible with
the report's overall optimality. The fractions come directly from the probabilities assigned to the four states.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}

The package evaluates both fixed reports under these directional errors; it does not search for them. Each returns
risk 11/60 at τ = 1/5. The input records the same finite teaching law used above.

```r
e <- matrix(c(NA,1/4,1/10,3/4,NA,1/4,9/10,3/4,NA),3,byrow=TRUE,dimnames=rep(list(c("A","B","C")),2))
input <- postrank::postrank_probabilities(e,criterion="priority",event="directional_error",zero_ties=TRUE,margin=0,source=list(kind="analytic_reference",description="ABC/ACB/BAC/CBA with masses .60/.15/.15/.10",conditioning="Complete fixed finite target law"),targets=c(priority="Fictional priority; larger is higher"))
vapply(list(c(A=1,B=1,C=2),c(A=1,B=2,C=2)),function(g) postrank::postrank_evaluate(g,input,weights=c(priority=1),tau=1/5)$primary_risk,numeric(1))
```

:::

Standalone: [coherence-finite](../../embed/coherence-finite.html), for example `?tau=.18`.

Related applications: [Coherence constraints on pairwise decisions](coherence.qmd), [The decision for an isolated pair](one-pair.qmd).
